International News · 16 Sources · 4 Regions

Daily Brief

The human cost of Russia's war in Ukraine came into stark focus today as leaked Russian government statistics analyzed by the BBC revealed nearly 500,000 Russian soldiers have died since 2022 [BBC], a figure the Kremlin declined to confirm, stating only the defence ministry can disclose casualties [France 24]. Meanwhile, Ukraine continued long-range strikes, claiming damage to five Russian military jets at an airfield 300km east of Moscow [BBC], while defending its weekend naval drone attacks on Russian vessels in Libya that killed two Libyan soldiers [RFI, Guardian]. On the economic front, the Trump administration announced sweeping new tariffs targeting 14 major trading partners including the EU, China, and India, based on a probe into excess industrial capacity [The Hindu, ABC Australia]. India faces a 25% tariff, second only to Vietnam's 35% [The Hindu]. In response to technological competition, the EU unveiled plans for a €50 billion fund to accelerate AI and quantum computing development, aiming to lead the world in quantum technology by 2030 [RFI, Le Monde]. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, reinstated after resigning over affairs including one with an alleged Chinese spy, apologized to staff and revealed he is in daily therapy [RNZ], while US Attorney General Todd Blanche deflected questions about federal investigations into the company [BBC].

Top Stories
01 Conflict

Leaked Russian Data Reveals Nearly 500,000 Soldiers Dead in Ukraine War

  • BBC analysis of 11 million leaked Rosstat death records shows at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the 2022 invasion began
  • Data was obtained by Belarusian hacker group Cyber Partisans and Ukraine's Silent Crow; BBC Russian matched 90% of records with its own confirmed death list
  • Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack but denied protected information was leaked; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only the defence ministry can officially report casualties
  • Military experts estimate true death toll could range between 530,000 and 700,000 when accounting for incomplete reporting

02 Economics

Trump Administration Announces Sweeping New Tariffs on 14 Major Trading Partners

  • New tariffs target China, EU, India, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, and eight other economies based on probe into excess industrial capacity
  • India faces 25% tariff (second-highest after Vietnam's 35%); tariffs for other partners range from 10-20%; Australia not affected
  • Tariffs stack on top of previous duties already imposed during Trump's second term; some Chinese goods face combined rate of 45%
  • Move comes despite midterm election setback and Reuters/Ipsos poll showing 62% of Americans support repealing tariffs

  • European Commission announced Sovereign Tech Equity Fund targeting €50 billion to boost AI and quantum computing capabilities
  • EU aims to lead the world in quantum technology by 2030 and avoid losing further ground to competitors
